title: OOM: pinned tensors after quantization migration — investigation notes
body:
Summary:

This is an SRE investigation note for a recurring OOM observed post-rolling upgrade of the 4-bit quantization migration (q4_0) for the well-known-cg model family on Hosted GPU cluster(s) in us-west1. Symptoms: hosts serving mixed q4 and q8 variants started reporting steady GPU memory growth over ~12-36 hours, culminating in OOM kills and degraded batch throughput. Root cause hypothesis centers on pinned device tensors (stale CUDA handles/KV pages) not being freed by the serving runtime during model swap / kernel switch paths — particularly when a request sequence triggers a rare codepath that pins and caches a model tensor for fast repeated inference but never releases on config-change.

Why this is different from prior kv/eviction incidents:
- The telemetry points to gradual per-host resident GPU memory growth even with normal QPS and without large batch spikes.
- No immediate eviction loop thrashing or batch queue stalls were observed in early stages.
- The allocation footprints correlate with model loader events (deploys/rollouts) and explicit quant-variant toggles, not with request KV cache size.

Timeline (concise):
- 2024-09-11 02:18 PDT: Automated rollout of q4_0 variant to 20% traffic in us-west1 (canary).
- 2024-09-11 06:00 PDT: First host reports +1.8GB GPU resident after ~6h. Alert: hostier1-gpu-12 memory slowly trending high (internal alert).
- 2024-09-11 18:00 PDT: Several hosts in the canary pool reached >85% GPU usage and experienced OOMs with kernel logs showing failed allocations.
- 2024-09-12 00:30 PDT: Rollback to q8 variant for canary. Temporary drop in memory growth, but two hosts remained high and were OOM-killed on 9/13.
- 2024-09-13 09:10 PDT: Investigation ticket INF-2142 opened.
- 2024-09-14 11:45 PDT: Repro locally on a dev host using model-loader toggles (see repro steps).

Observed signals / evidence: (raw snippets)
- nvidia-smi snapshots show persistent CUDA allocations tied to PIDs still running in the serving process even after model switch.
- /proc/<pid>/smaps and pmap show GPU-resident pages not freed until process restart.
- Serving runtime debug logs (model_loader DEBUG): "pinning tensor object id=0x7f9b2a1c event=model_swap" repeated but no matching unpin.
- Allocation trace from debug build: allocate_gpu_buffer(size=XXMB) -> pinned=true -> stash->global_cache[variant_key] but on reload code path stash removal missing.

Repro steps (dev + minimal):
1) Checkout PR branch with debug symbols: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime@pr/4789
2) Start single-host runtime with test_model A (q8) on empty cache, QPS low.
3) Issue a traffic pattern: 30s warmup of small requests, then 2 large-context requests (len>1024) that trigger kv-prefetch and kernel-selection path.
4) Trigger model variant swap via admin API to q4 variant (simulates rollout).
5) Continue issuing repeat requests; observe resident GPU memory with nvidia-smi.
6) Repeat swap back to q8 and watch for heap not decreasing (requires ~10 iterations to reliably reproduce).

Workarounds discovered during incident response:
- Short-term: pin-and-restart. Rebooting the process/host reclaims memory. For hosts where we could cordon and restart containers sequentially, outages were limited.
- Medium-term: disable aggressive model-variant rollouts for q4 on affected fleets; route critical production traffic away from mixed-variant pools.
- Instrumentation: enabled additional model_loader DEBUG logging and a periodic scan that logs stash sizes and number of pinned objects per process to CloudWatch.

Hypothesis (detailed):
When model-variant kernel selection switches between quantization-specific kernels (q8 <-> q4), the runtime performs an optimization: it pins a small set of transformed tensors (prefetched KV blocks, attention kernels, small fused-conv buffers) to the device and stores them in an LRU-like stash keyed by (model-id, variant, seq-len-bucket). During normal steady-state the stash limit and eviction path work. However, during variant swap the code path that invalidates stash entries assumes that the variant namespace is monotonic: a deletion call is made, but if the deletion occurs concurrently with a background refill (race between the swap routine and async prefetch completion), the stash may retain a reference count that is never decremented. Concurrency + refcounting bug prevents destructor path from running -> pinned device memory leakage.

Key logs & snippets (sanitized):
- TRACE model_loader: stash.insert(key=q4-1024, obj=Tensor{id=0x7f9b2a1c, pinned=true})
- TRACE prefetch_worker: completed_fetch id=0x7f9b2a1c -> put_in_stash
- WARN model_swap: invalidate_namespace(q8->q4) issued
- TRACE stash: decrement_ref id=0x7f9b2a1c -> refcount now 2
- (missing) TRACE stash: decrement_ref id=0x7f9b2a1c -> refcount now 1/0 (expected, but not present)
- On memory surge: ERROR cuda_runtime: out_of_memory when allocating 150MB buffer

Proposed immediate remediation (actions for on-call):
- If you see steady GPU resident growth >100MB/hr after a rollout: 1) drain host from LB, 2) rotate container (graceful shutdown) to force stash destructors, 3) mark host for short-interval memory-monitoring on restart.
- Add a temporary dynconfig to disable stash pinning for mix-variant pools (feature gate). This prevents pinning behavior until bugfix is deployed.

Proposed medium-term fixes (eng work):
- Patch stash reference management: ensure atomic refcount adjustments with compare-and-swap and ensure that invalidation waits for in-flight prefetch completions or cancels them cleanly. Link PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4789 (WIP).
- Add a defensive periodic GC that walks stash entries and forcibly frees any pinned tensors older than X minutes when memory pressure flagged.
- Expand telemetry: expose per-process pinned-tensor count and total pinned bytes to the metrics pipeline (prom metric: serving_pinned_tensors_total and serving_pinned_bytes).
- Add a pre-deployment test harness that stresses variant swap while measuring resident growth over N cycles. This should be part of release gating for quantization rollout.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Is stash pinning still providing enough latency benefit on p99 to justify complexity? (product/perf team to weigh).
- What is an acceptable pinned bytes budget per host? (SRE to propose default).
- Should we consider per-tenant pin budgets as well to isolate noisy tenants?

Action items (owners + ETA):
- (Priya) Add emergency dynconfig to disable stash pinning for mixed-variant pools — ETA: 1 day.
- (Marco) Draft and land atomic refcount fix + unit tests — ETA: 2 weeks (PR #4789).
- (Tasha) Add stash GC and metrics instrumentation to dev branch — ETA: 3 weeks.
- (Ethan) Add variant-swap stress test to CI harness and run against staging fleet — ETA: 2 weeks.

Notes to on-call responders (quick checklist):
- Detect: look for serving_pinned_bytes_total > 1GB or nvidia-smi persistent allocation patterns.
- Triage: check recent rollouts (admin audit trail), correlate host memory delta with model_loader events.
- Mitigate: cordon host, restart process, roll back variant toggles if needed.
- Post-incident: attach heap profile and model_loader logs to the INF-2142 ticket.

Appendix (quick commands):
- Check GPU resident: watch -n 5 nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv
- Dump stash counts: curl -s http://localhost:9001/debug/stash | jq .counts
- Force gc (temporary endpoint): curl -X POST http://localhost:9001/admin/force-stash-gc

End of note.

Record kept as a working doc; will convert to a runbook entry once fixes are in review and the temp dynconfig is applied.

Draft SLA impact blurb (for incident report):
- Impact window: ~2024-09-11 06:00 - 2024-09-13 14:30 PDT
- Customers affected: small fraction of latency-sensitive hosted API tenants routed to mixed-variant canary pools (~0.4% of total requests during window).
- User-visible: elevated 5xx rate on 2% of calls for affected tenants during peak reclamation windows.

Recorded by: Priya Nair (on-call SRE)
